methodology.partisan_lean: 5% 2016 + 20% 2020 + 75% 2024 district/state presidential margin, each centred on that year's national D-R margin
methodology.national_environment: 35-day generic-ballot poll average with exponential recency decay, sample-size and pollster-quality weighting; partisan-sponsored polls downweighted
methodology.race_polling: nominee-matched polls from the last 55 days blended with the prior; weight rises sub-linearly with poll count and is capped
methodology.probabilities: normal-error race model plus 30,000 correlated Monte Carlo chamber simulations
methodology.qualitative_news: not an input to numerical probabilities
methodology.senate_control: Democratic caucus requires 51 seats because the vice president is Republican

provenance.note: MIDTERM SIGNALS consumes factual/curated inputs from the upstream data repository, not its forecast outputs. Numerical transformations and simulations are performed here.

limitations: This is a transparent baseline model, not a claim of certainty.
Candidate-quality effects beyond incumbency are not yet separately estimated.
Third-party and ranked-choice transfer behaviour is simplified in the chamber model.
Race polls are used only when the poll matchup matches the current major-party nominees; missing polling remains missing.
The model can be wrong together across many races; correlated national error is therefore simulated explicitly.
